newsitem.title: USA: Calif. hydropower dam flows increased due to rain.
newsitem.headline: Calif. hydropower dam flows increased due to rain.

text.p: Flows through hydroelectric dams in central and northern California are being increased due to heavy rain this week and a new storm expected to hit the region Friday evening, regional sources said Thursday.

"The reservoirs are starting to get full again. We are trying to get as much water out as possible before the next storm without getting to a level where levees are damaged," said a spokesman at the California River Forecast Center.

He noted that this week's storms brought snow to elevations as low as 5,000 to 6,000 feet, but a weather system forecast to arrive this weekend is expected to be warmer, possibly creating higher runoff.
A new rainstorm is forecast to arrive Friday evening, and could continue through early next week.
A spokeswoman for the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (BuRec) in Sacramento said flows at both the Shasta Dam, on the Sacramento River, and Folsom Dam, on the American River, are being increased.
Flows at Shasta are now running at 36 thousand cubic feet per second (kcfs), up from 30 kcfs earlier Thursday.
Folsom Dam flows are at 36 kcfs, compared with 28 kcfs earlier, the spokeswoman said.
BuRec operates 12 hydropower plants in the district comprised of California, southern Oregon and western Nevada, which have total power generation capacity of 5,000 gigawatt hours.
